1.contenido: 1. The truth that sets people free is a gift from Jesus Christ ( [+[0]+] ). The search for truth is a demand of man's nature, while ignorance keeps him in a condition of slavery. Indeed, man cannot be truly free if he does not receive light on the central questions of his existence and in particular on the question of knowing where he comes from and where he is going. He becomes free when God gives himself to him as a Friend, according to the word of the Lord: «I no longer call you servants, because the servant does not know what his master is doing; but I call you friends, because everything that I have heard from the Father I have made known to you » ( [+[1]+] ). Liberation from the alienation of sin and death is realized in man when Christ, who is the Truth, becomes the "way" for him ([+[2]+]).

2.contenido: 2. Moved by a love without measure, God wanted to approach man who seeks his own identity and walk with him ( [+[0]+] ). He has freed him from the snares of the "father of lies" ([+[1]+]) and has introduced him into his intimacy so that he may find there, superabundantly, his full truth and his true freedom. This plan of love conceived by the "Father of light" ([+[2]+]), carried out by the Son who conquers death ([+[3]+]), is incessantly updated by the Spirit who leads "towards full venity" ([+[4]+]).

3.contenido: 3. The truth has in itself a unifying force: it frees men from the isolation and oppositions in which they find themselves locked by ignorance of the truth and, while opening the way to God, it unites them with each other. Christ destroyed the wall of separation that had made them alien to the promise of God and the communion of the Covenant ( [+[0]+] ). He sends into the hearts of believers His Spirit, through whom we are all “one” in Him ([+[1]+]). Thus we become, thanks to the new birth and the anointing of the Holy Spirit ([+[2]+]), the new and unique People of God who, with the various vocations and charisms, have the mission of preserving and transmitting the gift of truth. Indeed, the entire church as "salt of the earth" and "light of the world" ([+[3]+]), must bear witness to the truth of Christ that sets people free.

4.contenido: 4. The people of God respond to this call "above all through a life of faith and charity and offering to God a sacrifice of praise." In more specific relation to the "life of faith", the Second Vatican Council specifies that "the totality of the faithful, who have received the anointing of the Holy Spirit ([+[0]+]), cannot be mistaken when they believe, and this peculiar prerogative of theirs is manifested through the supernatural sense of faith of the entire people, when, 'from the bishops to the last laymen', they give their universal consent in matters of faith and customs"[2].

5.contenido: 5. To exercise their prophetic function in the world, the people of God must constantly awaken or "rekindle" their life of faith ([+[0]+]), especially through an increasingly profound reflection, guided by the Holy Spirit, on the content of faith itself and through an effort to demonstrate its rationality to those who ask it to account for it ([+[1]+]). For this mission the Spirit of truth grants, to faithful of all orders, special graces granted "for common use" ([+[2]+]).

6.contenido: 6. Among the vocations raised in this way by the Spirit in the church, that of the theologian stands out, who has the special function of achieving, in communion with the Magisterium, an increasingly deeper understanding of the Word of God contained in the inspired Scripture and transmitted by the living tradition of the church.

7.contenido: 7. The work of the theologian responds in this way to the dynamism present in faith itself: by its very nature the Truth wants to communicate, because man has been created to perceive the truth and desires in the deepest part of himself to know it in order to find himself in it and discover his salvation there ([+[0]+]). For this reason the Lord has sent his apostles to convert all peoples into "disciples" and preach to them ([+[1]+]). Theology that investigates the "reason of faith" and offers it as an answer to those who seek it, constitutes an integral part of obedience to this command, because men cannot become disciples if they are not presented with the truth contained in the word of faith ([+[2]+]).

8.contenido: 8. Since the object of theology is the Truth, the living God and his plan of salvation revealed in Jesus Christ, the theologian is called to intensify his life of faith and to always unite scientific research and prayer[4]. Thus you will be more open to the "supernatural sense of faith" on which you depend and which will appear to you as a sure rule to guide your reflection and measure the seriousness of your conclusions.

9.contenido: 9. Over the centuries, theology has progressively become a true scientific knowledge. Consequently, it is necessary for the theologian to be attentive to the epistemological demands of his discipline, to the requirements of critical rigor and, therefore, to the rational control of each of the stages of his research. But the critical demand cannot be identified with the critical spirit that is born rather from motivations of an affective nature or from prejudices. The theologian must discern within himself the origin and motivations of his critical attitude and allow his gaze to be purified by faith. Theological work requires a spiritual effort of righteousness and sanctification.

10.contenido: 10. The revealed truth, although it transcends human reason, is in deep harmony with it. This presupposes that reason is by its very nature ordered to truth so that, illuminated by faith, it can penetrate the meaning of revelation. Contrary to the statements of many philosophical currents, but in accordance with the right way of thinking that finds confirmation in Scripture, the capacity of human reason to reach the truth must be recognized, as well as its metaphysical capacity to know God from what is created[5].

11.contenido: 11. The theologian, without ever forgetting that he is also a member of the people of God, must respect him and commit to giving him a teaching that does not harm the doctrine of faith in the slightest.

12.contenido: 12. Freedom of investigation, to which the community of scientists tends precisely as one of its most precious assets, means willingness to accept the truth as it is presented at the end of the investigation, in which no element foreign to the demands of a method that corresponds to the object studied must have intervened.

13.contenido: 13. "God graciously arranged that everything he had revealed for the salvation of men would remain complete forever and be transmitted to all generations"[8]. He gave to his Church, by the gift of the Holy Spirit, a participation in his own infallibility[9]. The people of God, thanks to the "supernatural sense of faith", enjoy this prerogative, under the guidance of the living magisterium of the Church, which, by the authority exercised in the name of Christ, is the only authentic interpreter of the Word of God. written or transmitted[10].

14.contenido: 14. As successors of the Apostles, the pastors of the Church "receive from the Lord... the mission of teaching all nations and of preaching the Gospel to every creature, so that all men may achieve salvation..."[11]. That's why. They are entrusted with the office of preserving, exposing and disseminating the Word of God, of which they are servants[12].

15.contenido: 15. In order to fully fulfill the office entrusted to them of teaching the Gospel and authentically interpreting revelation, Jesus Christ promised the pastors of the Church the assistance of the Holy Spirit. He especially gave them the charisma of infallibility for that which refers to matters of faith and customs. The exercise of this charisma takes various forms. It is exercised, in particular, when the bishops, in union with their visible head, in a collegial act, as happens in ecumenical councils, proclaim a doctrine, or when the Roman Pontiff, exercising his function as Supreme Pastor and Doctor of all Christians, proclaims a doctrine "ex cathedra"[13].

16.contenido: 16. The office of holy preservation and faithful exposition of the deposit of divine revelation implies, by its very nature, that the Magisterium can propose "in a definitive manner"[14] statements that, although not contained in the truths of faith, are nevertheless closely linked to them, in such a way that the definitive character of these statements derives, in the last analysis, from Revelation itself[15].

17.contenido: 17. Divine assistance is also given to the successors of the Apostles, who teach in communion with the successor of Peter, and, in particular, to the Roman Pontiff, Pastor of the entire church when. Without reaching an infallible definition and without pronouncing in a "definitive manner", in the exercise of ordinary teaching they propose a teaching that leads to a better understanding of Revelation in matters of faith and customs, and they offer moral directives derived from this teaching.

18.contenido: 18. The Roman Pontiff fulfills his universal mission with the help of the organizations of the Roman Curia, and in particular of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith with regard to the doctrine on faith and morals. From which it follows that the documents of this Congregation, expressly approved by the Pope, participate in the ordinary magisterium of the successor of Peter[18].

19.contenido: 19. In particular Churches, it is the bishop's responsibility to guard and interpret the Word of God and to judge with authority what is in accordance with him or not. The teaching of each bishop, taken individually, is exercised in communion with that of the Roman Pontiff Pastor of the universal church and with the other bishops scattered throughout the world or gathered in an ecumenical Council. This communion is a condition of its authenticity.

20.contenido: 20. The pastoral task of the Magisterium. which has the purpose of ensuring that the people of God remain in the truth that sets them free, is a complex and diversified reality. The theologian, who is also committed to the service of truth, to remain faithful to his office, must take into account the mission of the Magisterium and collaborate with it. How can this collaboration be understood? How is it done specifically and what obstacles can it encounter? This is what now needs to be examined more closely.

21.contenido: 21. The living Magisterium of the Church and theology, even with different functions, ultimately have the same goal: to preserve the people of God in the truth that sets them free and to make them the "light of the nations." This service to the ecclesial community puts the theologian in a reciprocal relationship with the Magisterium. The latter authentically teaches the doctrine of the Apostles and, taking advantage of the theological work, rejects objections and distortions of the faith, also proposing with the authority received from Jesus Christ new insights, explanations and applications of the revealed doctrine. Theology, on the other hand, reflexively acquires an ever deeper understanding of the Word of God, contained in Scripture and faithfully transmitted by the living tradition of the Church under the guidance of the Magisterium, strives to clarify this teaching of Revelation in the face of the demands of reason and, finally, gives it an organic and systematic form[20].

22.contenido: 22. The collaboration between the theologian and the Magisterium is carried out especially when the latter receives the canonical mission or the mandate to teach. This then becomes, in a certain sense, a participation in the work of the Magisterium to which it is linked by a legal bond. The deontological rules that in themselves and with evidence derive from the service of the word of God are corroborated by the commitment acquired by the theologian when accepting his office and when making the profession of faith and the oath of fidelity[21].

23.contenido: 23. When the Magisterium of the Church pronounces itself in an infallible manner, solemnly declaring that a doctrine is contained in Revelation, the adherence that is requested is that of theological faith. This adherence extends to the teaching of the ordinary and universal magisterium when it proposes to believe a doctrine of faith as of divine revelation.

24.contenido: 24. Finally, in order to serve the people of God in the best possible way, particularly by warning them in relation to dangerous opinions that can lead to error, the Magisterium can intervene on debatable matters in which they are involved, together with sure principles, conjectural and contingent elements. Often only after a certain time is it possible to make a distinction between what is necessary and what is contingent.

25.contenido: 25. Even when collaboration develops under the best conditions, it is not excluded that some tensions may arise between the theologian and the Magisterium. The meaning given to the latter and the spirit with which they are faced are not unimportant realities: if the tensions do not arise from a feeling of hostility and opposition, they can represent a factor of dynamism and a stimulus that incites the Magisterium and the theologians to fulfill their respective functions by practicing dialogue.

26.contenido: 26. In dialogue a double rule must prevail: when the communion of faith is called into question, the principle of "unitas veritatis" applies; When divergences persist that do not call it into question, "unitas caritatis" must be safeguarded.

27.contenido: 27. Although the doctrine of faith is not in question, the theologian should not present his opinions or his divergent hypotheses as if they were indisputable conclusions. This discretion is required by respect for the truth, as well as respect for the people of God ( [+[0]+] ). For these same reasons, it must renounce an untimely public expression of them.

28.contenido: 28. The above has a particular application in the case of the theologian who finds serious difficulties, for reasons that seem well-founded, in accepting a magisterial teaching that is not irreformable.

29.contenido: 29. In any case, there cannot be a lack of a fundamental attitude of willingness to loyally accept the teaching of the Magisterium, which is imposed on every believer in the name of obedience of faith. The theologian must therefore strive to understand this teaching in its content, in its reasons and in its motives. To this task you must devote deep and patient reflection, willing to review your own opinions and examine the objections raised by your colleagues.

30.contenido: 30. If the difficulties persist despite a loyal effort, it is the duty of the theologian to make the teaching authorities aware of the problems raised by the teaching itself, the justifications proposed for it or also the way in which it has been presented. He will do it with an evangelical spirit, with the deep desire to resolve difficulties. Their objections will then be able to contribute to true progress, stimulating the Magisterium to propose the teaching of the Church in a more profound and better-argued way.

31.contenido: 31. It may happen that, at the end of a serious examination carried out with the desire to listen without reluctance to the teaching of the Magisterium, the difficulty remains, because the arguments in the opposite direction seem prevalent to the theologian. Faced with a statement to which you feel you cannot give your intellectual support, your duty is to remain willing to examine the problem more deeply.

32.contenido: 32. On several occasions the Magisterium has drawn attention to the serious inconveniences that those attitudes of systematic opposition bring to the communion of the Church, which even constitute organized groups[25]. In the apostolic exhortation Paterna cum benevolentia, Paul VI presented a diagnosis that retains all its relevance. Now we want to speak in particular of that public attitude of opposition to the Magisterium of the Church, also called "dissent", which must be distinguished from the situation of personal difficulty, which was discussed above. The phenomenon of dissent can have various forms and its remote or proximate causes are multiple.

33.contenido: 33. Dissent can have various aspects. In its most radical form, it seeks to change the church according to a model of protest inspired by what is done in political society. It is increasingly believed that the theologian would only be obliged to adhere to the infallible teaching of the Magisterium, while, on the other hand, the doctrines proposed without the intervention of the charisma of infallibility would not have any obligatory character, leaving the individual completely free to adhere or not, thus adopting the perspective of a kind of theological positivism. The theologian, therefore, would be free to question or reject the non-infallible teaching of the Magisterium, especially with regard to particular norms. Furthermore, with this critical opposition it would contribute to the progress of the doctrine.

34.contenido: 34. The justification for dissent is generally supported by various arguments, two of which are more fundamental in nature. The first is of a hermeneutical order: the documents of the Magisterium would be nothing more than the reflection of an opinionable theology. The second resorts to theological pluralism, sometimes taken to a relativism that endangers the integrity of the faith: magisterial interventions would have their origin in one theology among many others, while no particular theology can claim to be universally imposed. Thus a kind of "parallel magisterium" of theologians arises, in opposition and rivalry with the authentic magisterium[27].

35.contenido: 35. Dissent sometimes appeals to a sociological argument, according to which the opinion of a large number of Christians would constitute a direct and adequate expression of the "supernatural sense of faith."

36.contenido: 36. The freedom of the act of faith does not justify the right to dissent. In reality, it in no way means freedom in relation to the truth, but rather the free self-determination of the person in accordance with their moral obligation to accept the truth. The act of faith is a voluntary act, since man, redeemed by Christ the Savior and called by Himself to filial adoption ([+[0]+]), cannot adhere to God, unless, attracted by the Father ([+[1]+]), he renders to God the rational homage of his faith ([+[2]+]). As the declaration Dignitatis humanoe[35] has recalled, no human authority has the right to intervene, by coercion or pressure, in this option that exceeds the limits of its competence. Respect for the right to religious freedom constitutes the foundation of respect for all human rights.

37.contenido: 37. By virtue of the divine mandate given to it in the Church, the Magisterium's mission is to propose the teaching of the Gospel, monitor its integrity and thus protect the faith of the people of God. To carry out this mandate he is sometimes forced to take onerous measures; for example when he withdraws a theologian, who separates himself from the doctrine of faith, the canonical mission or the mandate to teach that he had entrusted to him, or when he declares that some writings do not agree with that doctrine. By acting in this way he wants to be faithful to his mission because he defends the right of the people of God to receive the message of the Church in its purity and integrity and, consequently, not to be disconcerted by a dangerous particular opinion.

38.contenido: 38. Finally, recourse to the argument of the duty to follow one's own conscience cannot legitimize dissent. First of all because this duty is exercised when conscience illuminates practical judgment in view of making a decision, while here it is about the truth of a doctrinal statement. Furthermore, because if the theologian, like every believer, must follow his own conscience, he is also obliged to form it. Conscience does not constitute an independent and infallible faculty, it is an act of moral judgment that refers to a responsible option. A right conscience is a conscience duly illuminated by faith and by the objective moral law, and also presupposes the rectitude of the will in the pursuit of true good.

39.contenido: 39. The church, which has its origin in the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit[39], is a mystery of communion, organized in accordance with the will of its founder around a hierarchy that has been established for the service of the Gospel and the people of God who live it. In the image of the members of the first community, all the baptized, with the charismas that are their own, must tend with a sincere heart towards a harmonious unity of doctrine, life and worship ([+[0]+]). This is a rule that comes from the very being of the church. Therefore, the criteria of conduct that have their reason for being in civil society or in the rules of operation of a democracy cannot be applied purely and simply to the latter. Even less so when it comes to relationships within the church, can it be inspired by the mentality of the environment ( [+[1]+] ). Asking the majority public opinion what it is appropriate to think or do, resorting to exerting pressure from public opinion against the Magisterium, claiming as a pretext a "consensus" of theologians, maintaining that the theologian is the prophetic spokesperson of a "base" or autonomous community that would therefore be the only source of truth, all of this denotes a serious loss of the sense of truth and the sense of church.

40.contenido: 40. The Church is "like a sacrament or sign and instrument of intimate union with God and of the unity of the entire human race"[40]. Therefore, seeking concord and communion means increasing the strength of your testimony and credibility; Giving in, however, to the temptation of dissent is to allow "ferments of infidelity to the Holy Spirit" to develop[41].

41.contenido: 41. Both must always keep in mind that Christ is the definitive Word of the Father ([+[0]+]) in whom, as Saint John of the Cross observes, "God has told us everything together and at once"[43] and who, as such, is the Truth that sets us free ([+[1]+]). The acts of adhesion and assent to the Word entrusted to the church under the guidance of the Magisterium ultimately refer to Him and enter the field of true freedom.

42.contenido: 42. The Virgin Mary, Mother and perfect image of the Church, has been proclaimed blessed since the beginning of the New Testament, due to her immediate and unhesitating adherence to the word of God ([+[0]+]), which she kept and meditated permanently in her heart ([+[1]+]). She has thus become a model and support for all the people of God entrusted to her maternal care. It shows him the path of welcoming and serving the Word and, at the same time, the ultimate goal that must never be lost sight of: the announcement to all men and the realization of the salvation brought to the world by his Son Jesus Christ.
